questions.stem: A Wisconsin supervising attorney has a vision impairment. What assistive-technology condition does the estate guidance state?
options: Any after-the-fact email suffices
Every impairment prevents remote work
Only a customer may provide legal supervision instead
The substitute must enable active real-time participation
questions.explanation: The footnote allows suitable substitution for audio or video.
feedback: The allowance still requires real-time participation.
The guide includes an accommodation.
Assistive technology does not replace the attorney role.
Correct. The footnote allows suitable substitution for audio or video.

questions.stem: A Wisconsin provider's conditions fail and its approval is revoked. What should a notary understand about the former approved listing?
options: The notary may self-approve the provider
The provider's advertisement overrides DFI action
Approval is conditional and can be revoked for noncompliance
An old screenshot guarantees permanent approval
questions.explanation: The guide expressly identifies revocation of provider approval.
feedback: Notaries cannot grant provider approval.
Advertising does not control approval.
Correct. The guide expressly identifies revocation of provider approval.
Conditional status can change.

questions.stem: A Wisconsin notary depends on a renewal reminder sent to an obsolete address. Which continuing obligation helps avoid this problem?
options: Use an old address until the next decade
Keep contact details current through the ten-day written reporting duty
Rely only on a stamp supplier's mailing list
Assume a reminder renews the term
questions.explanation: The handbook links current information with expiration-notice delivery.
feedback: The contact change has a prompt deadline.
Correct. The handbook links current information with expiration-notice delivery.
That does not update DFI.
Renewal requires action.

questions.stem: A Wisconsin notary says the handbook's optional ordinary journal rule permits deleting ordinary RON videos. What correction is needed?
options: The remote audiovisual recording duty is distinct from an ordinary optional journal
All recordkeeping is optional everywhere
Every ordinary paper appointment must be video recorded
Only the vendor decides whether law applies
questions.explanation: Different record obligations apply to remote acts.
feedback: Correct. Different record obligations apply to remote acts.
The remote guidance requires recording and retention.
That is not the stated ordinary journal rule.
The legal remote duty still controls.

questions.stem: A Wisconsin nonattorney notary is asked whether a corporation should choose a trust or a power of attorney, then to notarize the choice. What boundary comes first?
options: The commission authorizes all document selection
A representative signature grants the notary a law license
A five-dollar fee permits legal advice
Do not provide the legal drafting or selection advice beyond the notary's authority
questions.explanation: The handbook's nonattorney limit applies before the ceremony.
feedback: It does not confer law-practice authority.
The customer's role does not license the notary.
The notarial fee does not expand professional authority.
Correct. The handbook's nonattorney limit applies before the ceremony.

questions.stem: A Wisconsin customer assumes the notary seal itself is the authentication needed by a foreign recipient. What separate step should be distinguished?
options: Backdate the act to avoid certification
The recipient's request automatically appoints the notary as state authenticator
The proper state authentication or apostille process for the destination
Stamp twice to create an apostille
questions.explanation: The tutorial describes a certificate attached to an already properly notarized record.
feedback: False dating does not supply authentication.
A customer cannot grant that authority.
Correct. The tutorial describes a certificate attached to an already properly notarized record.
Repeated impressions do not issue state authentication.

questions.stem: A Wisconsin applicant obtains issuance notice after a planned appointment date and asks to certify the earlier meeting as if commissioned then. What controls?
options: Ask the first customer to ratify state authority
Authority must exist when the notarial act is actually performed
Backdate using the new commission
Use only the bond's purchase date
questions.explanation: Issuance later does not authorize a prior uncommissioned act.
feedback: A customer cannot retroactively commission the applicant.
Correct. Issuance later does not authorize a prior uncommissioned act.
That misstates authority and event timing.
Coverage purchase alone does not establish commission issuance.

cards.title: Applicant connection
cards.front: What residence is required for the ordinary four-year route?
cards.rule: The applicant is a United States resident under the stated eligibility conditions.
cards.boundary: Other age, education, familiarity and trust conditions also apply.
cards.mixup: Do not substitute a Wisconsin-only residence rule for the published U.S. residence condition.

cards.title: Education baseline
cards.front: What education condition is listed?
cards.rule: At least the equivalent of an eighth-grade education.
cards.boundary: Examination passage addresses familiarity with duties.
cards.mixup: A purchased study course does not itself establish every qualification.

cards.title: Final examination
cards.front: Who takes the ordinary final?
cards.rule: Both new and renewing four-year applicants pass at least ninety percent.
cards.boundary: The test is taken within the stated one-year recency period.
cards.mixup: Prior notarial experience does not remove the stated renewal exam.

cards.title: Tutorial flexibility
cards.front: Are all chapter readings and quizzes mandatory?
cards.rule: Knowledgeable applicants may go directly to the final.
cards.boundary: The final itself remains required for the four-year route.
cards.mixup: Optional readings do not make the assessment optional.

cards.title: Single sitting
cards.front: How is the current final session completed?
cards.rule: Complete the thirty-question final in one sitting.
cards.boundary: The instructions say it cannot be saved and resumed.
cards.mixup: Do not infer a numeric timer from the single-sitting condition.

cards.title: Passing evidence
cards.front: What does the applicant preserve after passing?
cards.rule: Save the browser certificate and upload it with the application evidence.
cards.boundary: DFI does not store the score or regenerate that certificate.
cards.mixup: A browser closing can lose the evidence even after a passing result.

cards.title: Four-year package
cards.front: What completes the ordinary filing materials?
cards.rule: Provide application information, oath, specific bond and required execution samples.
cards.boundary: Follow current official upload instructions.
cards.mixup: Fee payment alone does not establish complete documentation.

cards.title: Issuance boundary
cards.front: When may an applicant begin acts?
cards.rule: After notice that the commission has issued.
cards.boundary: Additional remote compliance still precedes remote services.
cards.mixup: A seal order or pending application does not establish active authority.

cards.title: Permanent attorney route
cards.front: Does law licensure alone commission an attorney?
cards.rule: The attorney applies for a permanent or ordinary commission and receives issuance notice.
cards.boundary: Permanent authority has separate good-standing evidence and no bond.
cards.mixup: Bar admission is not automatic notarial appointment.

cards.title: Transition calendar
cards.front: How is the November 2026 system notice used?
cards.rule: The opened page schedules the new system for November 16 at 7 a.m. Central.
cards.boundary: On the November 14 check date this is a future transition notice.
cards.mixup: A scheduled system change does not itself waive examination or revoke commissions.

cards.title: Specific bond
cards.front: What coverage supports the four-year commission?
cards.rule: A separate specific five-hundred-dollar surety bond.
cards.boundary: The employer's blanket bond does not fulfill it.
cards.mixup: Optional E&O is a separate product.

cards.title: Bond beneficiary
cards.front: Who does the statutory bond protect?
cards.rule: It protects a party harmed by the notary's misconduct or neglect within its coverage.
cards.boundary: Damages beyond the coverage can remain personally payable.
cards.mixup: Bonding is not complete immunity for the notary.

cards.title: Licensed surety
cards.front: Where is the bond obtained?
cards.rule: From an insurance or surety company qualified to write Wisconsin surety coverage.
cards.boundary: DFI does not supply or recommend a bonding company.
cards.mixup: A low price does not establish provider licensure.

cards.title: Term coverage
cards.front: How long does the filed ordinary bond run?
cards.rule: It remains with the full four-year commission term.
cards.boundary: The handbook states the filed bond cannot be cancelled.
cards.mixup: Replacing a stamp does not end the bond period.

cards.title: Permanent bonding
cards.front: Is a bond required for the permanent attorney commission?
cards.rule: The permanent route does not require the ordinary surety bond.
cards.boundary: That route still requires its application and good-standing evidence.
cards.mixup: No-bond status does not waive the tangible-record seal.

cards.title: Seal wording
cards.front: Which text identifies the ordinary official device?
cards.rule: Notary Public, State of Wisconsin and the notary name with the current legal last name in full.
cards.boundary: The permitted shape and size are flexible.
cards.mixup: An employer logo does not replace the required wording.

cards.title: Filed-name signature
cards.front: How does the signature relate to the seal?
cards.rule: Sign exactly the name shown on the filed official device.
cards.boundary: A shortened first name can be used when properly selected and filed.
cards.mixup: Do not add an unfiled different name in parentheses.

cards.title: Tangible impression
cards.front: Who must seal tangible-record acts?
cards.rule: All commissioned notaries, including permanent attorney-notaries.
cards.boundary: Use a legible impression with the proper certificate.
cards.mixup: Permanent duration does not exempt the device requirement.

cards.title: Multiple devices
cards.front: Can one notary use an embosser and ink stamp?
cards.rule: Both may be used after required samples are filed and DFI confirmation is received.
cards.boundary: The same filed identity applies to each device.
cards.mixup: Buying the second device does not authorize immediate use.

cards.title: Optional E&O
cards.front: How is optional E&O handled?
cards.rule: It may help with covered legal fees and damages and stays in personal records.
cards.boundary: It is not filed as the required notary bond.
cards.mixup: The policy does not renew state authority.

cards.title: Venue event
cards.front: What location goes into the venue?
cards.rule: The place where the notary performs the act.
cards.boundary: The home county and document destination can differ.
cards.mixup: A preprinted venue should not misstate the actual location.

cards.title: Earlier execution
cards.front: How is an earlier signature acknowledged?
cards.rule: The appearing individual confirms their earlier knowing voluntary execution.
cards.boundary: The notary uses the actual acknowledgment date.
cards.mixup: The certificate does not claim the notary watched yesterday's signing.

cards.title: Sworn statement
cards.front: What extra commitment is in the jurat procedure?
cards.rule: The signer specifically swears or affirms that the statements are true.
cards.boundary: The handbook also requires real-time witnessing of signing.
cards.mixup: A signature acknowledgment alone does not supply the pledge.

cards.title: Affirmation
cards.front: What nonreligious truth pledge is available?
cards.rule: An affirmation supplies the solemn truth commitment.
cards.boundary: It carries perjury consequences like the oath.
cards.mixup: A secular form is not an informal waiver of truthfulness.

cards.title: Unsworn witnessing
cards.front: What defines the unsworn-signature ceremony?
cards.rule: Identify the appearing person and observe actual signing.
cards.boundary: Use certificate language describing that observed event.
cards.mixup: The act does not silently include a truth oath.

cards.title: Representative role
cards.front: What additional confirmation does the representative give?
cards.rule: Confirmation of due authority to sign for the represented person or entity.
cards.boundary: The certificate includes the representative capacity.
cards.mixup: The notary does not guarantee the entity's financial condition.

cards.title: Interest screen
cards.front: Whose interests are screened?
cards.rule: The notary's, spouse's and domestic partner's stated party or direct beneficial interests.
cards.boundary: The conflict is not removed by a fee waiver.
cards.mixup: A company title does not automatically eliminate a personal benefit.

cards.title: Vital records
cards.front: Where are vital-record copies appropriately obtained?
cards.rule: From the official vital-record custodian.
cards.boundary: The handbook prohibits the notary's certified or uncertified copying and notarization of vital-record photocopies.
cards.mixup: A sworn cover description does not erase the record-specific warning.

cards.title: Separate jurat
cards.front: How can a jurat fit when the page is full?
cards.rule: Use a securely related attached page with the identifying cross-references the handbook advises.
cards.boundary: The certificate still describes the actual act.
cards.mixup: A loose pre-signed blank is not the attached completed jurat.

cards.title: Authentication stage
cards.front: What follows proper notarization for some destinations?
cards.rule: The appropriate state authentication or apostille process.
cards.boundary: Identify the destination country for the Convention-related route.
cards.mixup: The notary seal itself is not a self-issued apostille.

cards.title: Contact reporting
cards.front: What deadline covers changed contact details?
cards.rule: Provide written notice to DFI within ten days, including email changes.
cards.boundary: Current details support receipt of expiration notices.
cards.mixup: Postal forwarding alone does not update the commission office.

cards.title: New-name use
cards.front: What precedes using a new notarial name and seal?
cards.rule: Submit the required change information before new-name and device usage.
cards.boundary: The signature must match the filed device identity.
cards.mixup: Social-media changes do not amend the official file.

cards.title: Prior-name continuation
cards.front: Can a changed-name notary use the former filed name during the term?
cards.rule: The tutorial permits it for the remainder of the current commission with exact signature-device matching.
cards.boundary: A later commission application uses the current legal last name.
cards.mixup: Continuation is not permission to mix old and new names freely.

cards.title: Additional sample
cards.front: What accompanies a new device sample under the handbook?
cards.rule: The signature, expiration and intended-use information identified by the handbook.
cards.boundary: Prior-use filing and confirmation still apply.
cards.mixup: A supplier receipt does not replace the execution sample.

cards.title: Lost-device notice
cards.front: What is the response to discovering loss or theft?
cards.rule: Immediately notify DFI in writing.
cards.boundary: Then follow the distinguishable replacement and filing process.
cards.mixup: Proof of an already forged act is not required before notice.

cards.title: Replacement distinction
cards.front: How should a lost-device replacement differ?
cards.rule: It has a different appearance from the former device.
cards.boundary: Submit its sample and await DFI confirmation before use.
cards.mixup: An identical unfiled device misses the described replacement process.

cards.title: Replacement certificate
cards.front: How is a commission certificate replaced?
cards.rule: Request it in writing with the stated ten-dollar fee.
cards.boundary: The replacement evidences the existing commission.
cards.mixup: It does not restart the four-year term.

cards.title: Filed public records
cards.front: What public-record treatment applies to filed commission papers?
cards.rule: The handbook says application and bond materials are subject to Wisconsin open-records law.
cards.boundary: Inspection and copying can explain commercial renewal solicitations.
cards.mixup: Private confidentiality assumptions do not determine filed-record status.

cards.title: Ordinary journal
cards.front: What is the ordinary journal status?
cards.rule: The handbook encourages an ordinary journal without making it a general mandate.
cards.boundary: Useful entries can preserve appointment details.
cards.mixup: This does not waive remote audiovisual recording duties.

cards.title: Record continuity
cards.front: What survives switching RON providers?
cards.rule: The notary's recording and retention responsibilities continue.
cards.boundary: Arrange retrieval and storage while completing the new provider's onboarding.
cards.mixup: Cancelling a subscription does not erase the legal retention period.

cards.title: Route selection
cards.front: Why identify the remote document category first?
cards.rule: Estate planning follows the special Part 3 process, while ordinary RON uses Part 2.
cards.boundary: Remote deposition oaths have their separately identified rule.
cards.mixup: A universal video workflow does not address all categories.

cards.title: Provider authority
cards.front: What makes an ordinary RON system usable?
cards.rule: It is approved for Wisconsin use and the notary completes its training and authorization.
cards.boundary: Multiple platforms require onboarding with each.
cards.mixup: A generic meeting subscription is not approval.

cards.title: Remote identity
cards.front: What technological proofing is identified?
cards.rule: Credential analysis and dynamic KBA are the two approved types described.
cards.boundary: Qualifying personal knowledge supplies the stated proofing exception.
cards.mixup: A passing notary exam does not verify a customer's remote identity.

cards.title: Record and certificate
cards.front: What connects the remote act to its record?
cards.rule: Confirm the same record and include the communication-technology statement in the certificate.
cards.boundary: Tamper evidence must reveal later changes.
cards.mixup: A similar filename alone does not establish the same record.

cards.title: Seven-year recording
cards.front: What is preserved after ordinary RON?
cards.rule: The audiovisual performance is retained at least seven years.
cards.boundary: Repositories may help, but the notary remains ultimately responsible.
cards.mixup: The ordinary optional journal does not replace this recording.

cards.title: Confidentiality
cards.front: Which separate release bases are described?
cards.rule: Separate written requester consent or the specified necessary legal-process disclosure.
cards.boundary: Retention alone does not authorize marketing use.
cards.mixup: A subscription payment is not separate written disclosure consent.

cards.title: Estate supervision
cards.front: Who oversees the special estate signing?
cards.rule: A Wisconsin attorney in good standing supervises and may also serve as notary if commissioned.
cards.boundary: The attorney completes the compliance affidavit.
cards.mixup: An ordinary provider account does not replace legal supervision.

cards.title: Estate locations
cards.front: Where are the notary and remote estate individual located?
cards.rule: Both must be physically in Wisconsin and make the described attestations.
cards.boundary: Ordinary RON has different signer-location treatment.
cards.mixup: A Wisconsin mailing address does not relocate a person across the border.

cards.title: Estate visible execution
cards.front: What does the estate individual present and declare?
cards.rule: Identify others present, display pages, make the age/document/voluntariness declarations and sign visibly.
cards.boundary: The notary and attorney observe the signing.
cards.mixup: A hidden signature below the camera misses a stated safeguard.

cards.title: Estate document handling
cards.front: What happens after the special remote estate communication?
cards.rule: Use a listed original-or-copy route, complete notarization, and send the document to the attorney for retention.
cards.boundary: The attorney completes the statutory compliance affidavit.
cards.mixup: An ordinary PDF download alone does not perform every estate step.

commission.summary: Wisconsin has an ordinary four-year route and a permanent route for qualifying Wisconsin attorneys. Ordinary first applicants and renewals take the required final examination and provide the prescribed application materials.

sections.heading: Prepare the ordinary file
sections.body: The ordinary eligibility conditions include United States residency, minimum age eighteen, the stated educational equivalency and qualifications for public trust. Study the official duties through the free tutorial or proceed directly to the required final if already knowledgeable. The current final has thirty questions, requires ninety percent and is completed in one sitting. Save the passing browser certificate because the instructions say the office cannot regenerate it.

sections.heading: Wait for issued authority
sections.body: Follow the current filing page for the online information, executed oath, specific bond and active seal/signature samples. Notice that the commission has issued precedes performing acts. Permanent attorney applicants have separate good-standing evidence and no ordinary bond, but must still apply and receive issuance. On the November 14 verification date, the filing page schedules a new system for November 16, 2026 at 7 a.m. Central, so consult the official entry when actually filing.

example.heading: An experienced renewal applicant
example.body: A long-serving Milwaukee notary prepares the next four-year application. Familiarity permits skipping readings and quizzes, but the current introduction still requires the final for renewals within its recency window. The applicant saves the passing evidence and completes the renewed materials instead of treating experience as an examination waiver.

keyFacts: Ordinary authority has a four-year term.
New and renewing four-year applicants take the final.
Current final passage is ninety percent or better.
Bar admission alone does not appoint an attorney as notary.

supplies.summary: A four-year Wisconsin commission uses a specific five-hundred-dollar surety bond and a compliant filed official device. Name consistency and prior filing matter whenever a device is used or added.

sections.heading: Distinguish the coverage products
sections.body: The ordinary bond is a separate notary surety bond, with a qualified Wisconsin provider and full-term coverage. An employment blanket bond does not substitute. Optional E&O can help with covered defense costs and damages but is kept in personal records and does not replace the statutory bond. The surety coverage protects the harmed public and does not cap all personal responsibility.

sections.heading: Match the device to filed execution
sections.body: Obtain the official seal or rubber stamp before completing the application as instructed. Include Notary Public, State of Wisconsin and the selected name with the current legal last name in full. The signature used for acts exactly matches the filed device name. All commissioned notaries, including attorneys, use the required tangible-record impression. Additional devices need samples and the prescribed filing and DFI confirmation before use.

example.heading: A second device for travel
example.body: A Green Bay notary wants a portable ink stamp in addition to an embosser. The new device uses the same filed identity and its sample is sent with the required change information before use. Buying from the same supplier as the embosser does not itself complete the agency process.

keyFacts: The ordinary bond amount is five hundred dollars.
A blanket employment bond is insufficient.
Permanent attorney commissions have no ordinary bond requirement.
The seal name includes the full current legal last name.

acts.summary: Choose the ceremony that matches the requested act and certificate. Wisconsin distinguishes acknowledgment, unsworn witnessing and sworn or affirmed statements, with separate conflict and record boundaries.

sections.heading: Complete the person-centered ceremony
sections.body: For acknowledgment, establish the lawful appearance, identity, understanding and knowing voluntary execution. An earlier signature can be acknowledged through the present procedure. Signature witnessing involves observed signing, and a sworn statement adds the specific truth pledge by oath or affirmation. The handbook requires real-time signing for the sworn-signature procedure and directs re-signing when necessary.

sections.heading: Record the event accurately
sections.body: Use the actual notarial location for venue and the actual event date. Sign and make the legible official impression with the proper certificate. A representative confirms due authority and the certificate identifies that role. Screen the notary, spouse and domestic partner conflicts. The handbook prohibits vital-record copying and notarization of vital-record photocopies and directs customers to official custodians. Nonattorney commissioning does not authorize drafting legal papers.

example.heading: Earlier agreement, current affidavit
example.body: A customer brings a previously signed private agreement for acknowledgment and an earlier signed affidavit for sworn verification. The first can be acknowledged through the present ceremony. For the affidavit, the notary administers the oath or affirmation and witnesses the required fresh signing. The certificates describe the different acts actually completed.

keyFacts: Venue follows the location of the notarial act.
Acknowledgment can concern an earlier signature.
A truth pledge belongs to the sworn procedure.
Representative execution requires the appropriate authority confirmation.

maintenance.summary: Wisconsin requires timely written contact updates and prior filing for new-name or device use. Journals, filed public records, replacement certificates and insurance have separate treatment.

sections.heading: Update the official usage record
sections.body: Report changed contact information, including email, in writing within ten days. Before using a new name and device, submit the required change form and samples. The tutorial permits continuing the former filed name for the remainder of the existing commission when the signature exactly matches the device, but a later commission uses the current legal last name. Additional devices use the stated prior filing and confirmation process.

sections.heading: Respond to loss and preserve useful evidence
sections.body: Immediately report a lost or stolen official device in writing. Order the directed different-appearance replacement, submit the required sample and wait for DFI confirmation before using it. A replacement commission certificate has its own written-request procedure. The ordinary journal is encouraged rather than generally mandated by the handbook, while remote audiovisual preservation has its own requirement. Filed commission application and bond papers are subject to the stated public-record framework.

example.heading: Move and loss in the same month
example.body: A Madison notary changes email and later discovers a missing stamp. The email update has the ten-day written notice rule, while the stamp loss calls for immediate written notice and the separate replacement workflow. Completing one notice does not automatically authorize a new device or update every other changed detail.

keyFacts: Contact changes have a ten-day written notice deadline.
Signature and filed device name stay consistent.
Device loss or theft requires immediate written notice.
An ordinary optional journal does not waive remote recording retention.

remote.summary: Wisconsin ordinary RON uses approved technology with provider-specific training and remote safeguards. Estate-planning acts use a distinct attorney-supervised procedure under section 140.147.

sections.heading: Arrange ordinary RON safeguards
sections.body: A commissioned notary obtains authorization and training with a suitable approved provider, then checks provider notification and the public database. Confirm identity through the prescribed route, the same record, tamper evidence and the communication-technology certificate statement. Preserve the audiovisual performance for at least seven years through a retrievable arrangement. The notary remains physically in Wisconsin and ultimately responsible for preservation and confidentiality.

sections.heading: Route estate planning correctly
sections.body: Identify a will, trust-related record, covered power of attorney or other listed estate-planning document before using an ordinary workflow. The special procedure needs a Wisconsin attorney in good standing supervising, real-time interactive communication and both notary and individual physically in Wisconsin. Follow the document presentation, declarations, visible execution, listed original/copy handling and attorney affidavit of compliance. Its technology treatment differs from ordinary approved-provider RON.

example.heading: One video request, two record types
example.body: A Wisconsin notary receives a commercial closing record and a personal health-care power of attorney. The limited real-estate context and the estate-planning category require careful routing under the guide. The ordinary vendor workflow cannot simply be applied to the health-care document without the special supervision, location and affidavit safeguards.

keyFacts: No additional state commission is required for remote work.
Ordinary RON requires approved technology and system training.
The ordinary remote recording minimum is seven years.
Estate remote execution has a separate attorney-supervised process.

articles.keyword: A Wisconsin name change during an existing term
articles.title: A Wisconsin name change during an existing term
articles.description: Keep prior-name continuation distinct from using a new filed device.
articles.h1: A Wisconsin name change during an existing term
articles.lede: A legal name change creates choices and filing duties that must remain consistent with the official signature.

sections.heading: Identify the current filed name
sections.body: A Madison notary changes their legal last name while holding an unexpired four-year commission. The tutorial permits continued use of the previous name for the remainder of that commission if the signature exactly matches the filed seal or stamp. This specific continuation option is relevant to the existing term and should be read before mixing old and new execution names.

sections.heading: File before new-name use
sections.body: If the notary chooses to use the new name and device, the tutorial directs completing the required Address/Name/Seal Change process before using them. A new stamp order and an employer personnel update do not supply the agency filing. The execution samples identify the notarial usage that is actually being placed in the official record.

sections.heading: Keep the signature consistent
sections.body: While using the prior filed device, the notary does not add a different new name in parentheses or a hyphenated form that no longer matches it. The tutorial expressly rejects that approach. A customer may recognize both names, but recognition does not change the official signature-device matching requirement for notarizations.

sections.heading: Prepare the next term correctly
sections.body: When the notary later applies for another commission, the application uses the current legal last name. The handbook distinguishes this future application from the limited continuation during an existing term. Check the device sample and intended execution name together so that renewal preparation does not carry an outdated naming choice into the new application.

sources.title: Wisconsin DFI Handbook pp.18-19; Tutorial Chapter 5

faqs.q: May the previous filed name continue during the existing term?
faqs.a: The tutorial permits that with exact signature-device matching.

faqs.q: Can a new different name simply be added in parentheses?
faqs.a: The tutorial says a different added name does not satisfy its matching rule.

articles.keyword: A Wisconsin missing stamp needs more than a replacement order
articles.title: A Wisconsin missing stamp needs more than a replacement order
articles.description: Follow immediate notice, distinguishable replacement and DFI confirmation.
articles.h1: A Wisconsin missing stamp needs more than a replacement order
articles.lede: The replacement workflow helps distinguish a new official device from one whose security was lost.

sections.heading: Respond to discovery
sections.body: A Milwaukee notary returns from a mobile appointment and discovers the stamp is missing. The tutorial directs immediate written notice to DFI. It does not make proof of a forged act a condition for reporting loss or theft. An internal note to a manager or a purchase order sent to a supplier addresses different tasks and does not notify the commission office.

sections.heading: Order a distinct device
sections.body: The replacement is to have a different appearance from the former device. It still contains the required wording and name, so a different appearance is not permission to omit Wisconsin, Notary Public or the filed personal identity. The design distinction helps separate the replacement device from the lost or stolen one in the official usage record.

sections.heading: Complete the prior-use process
sections.body: After receipt, complete the required change filing and submit the sample before using the replacement. The current tutorial says use follows confirmation from DFI, while the handbook likewise directs waiting for notification that the new device may be used. Delivery of a well-made replacement therefore does not complete every step of the replacement procedure.

sections.heading: Resolve later developments
sections.body: If the former stamp later turns up, do not assume that the discovery itself updates the loss and replacement information on file. The published process ties authorized usage to the filed devices and agency notice. Clarify the status with DFI before treating both devices as available, while keeping the personal execution name and required samples consistent.

sources.title: Wisconsin DFI Handbook p.19; Tutorial Chapter 5

faqs.q: Is a supplier order the required written notice?
faqs.a: No. The notice is directed to DFI.

faqs.q: Can the replacement be used immediately on delivery?
faqs.a: Complete the required filing and receive DFI confirmation before use.

articles.keyword: Wisconsin bond coverage and optional E&O serve different roles
articles.title: Wisconsin bond coverage and optional E&O serve different roles
articles.description: Understand the ordinary bond without treating its amount as a liability ceiling.
articles.h1: Wisconsin bond coverage and optional E&O serve different roles
articles.lede: The handbook describes a public-protection surety bond and separate optional coverage for the notary.

sections.heading: Recognize the required product
sections.body: An employer offers its branch employee a general blanket bond and says it should cover notarial work. The Wisconsin handbook requires a separate specific five-hundred-dollar notary surety bond for the four-year route. Employment coverage does not replace that product merely because it may refer to honesty or employee conduct in broader business operations.

sections.heading: Check the provider and term
sections.body: The bond comes from an insurance or surety company qualified to write the required Wisconsin coverage. The ordinary bond runs with the full commission term, and the handbook states that a filed bond cannot be cancelled during it. DFI does not provide bonding or recommend a seller, so the applicant obtains the coverage through a qualified source.

sections.heading: Understand the protection limit
sections.body: The bond protects a harmed party for covered misconduct or neglect within the amount of the surety obligation. The handbook explains that damages beyond five hundred dollars can be the notary's personal responsibility. The coverage amount therefore does not provide a universal ceiling on consequences arising from an improper notarization.

sections.heading: Treat optional insurance separately
sections.body: An Errors and Omissions policy is optional and may help with covered legal fees and damages if the notary is sued. The handbook says it is different from the bond and is kept in personal records instead of filed with the commission materials. Neither product removes the identity, ceremony, certificate or impartiality duties that apply to the actual act.

faqs.q: Does an employment blanket bond replace the notary bond?
faqs.a: The handbook requires a separate specific bond.

faqs.q: Does five hundred dollars cap all personal responsibility?
faqs.a: No. The handbook states that excess damages can remain the notary's responsibility.

articles.keyword: An earlier Wisconsin signature can lead to different ceremonies
articles.title: An earlier Wisconsin signature can lead to different ceremonies
articles.description: Distinguish acknowledgment from a statement that must be signed and sworn in real time.
articles.h1: An earlier Wisconsin signature can lead to different ceremonies
articles.lede: A document already bearing a signature does not determine which act occurred at the current appointment.

sections.heading: Read the requested certificate
sections.body: A Green Bay customer brings a previously signed agreement and an affidavit. The agreement requests acknowledgment, while the affidavit says subscribed and sworn before the notary. The handbook requires the proper ceremony and written certificate for the actual requested act. Treating the printed words as interchangeable can result in certifying a procedure that was never performed.

sections.heading: Acknowledge earlier execution
sections.body: For the agreement, the signer appears lawfully and confirms the earlier signature was made knowingly and voluntarily for the intended purpose. The handbook permits this earlier-signature acknowledgment. The certificate uses the current acknowledgment date and venue and does not falsely state that the notary observed yesterday's original signing.

sections.heading: Complete the sworn procedure
sections.body: For the affidavit, the handbook requires a specific truth pledge by oath or affirmation and real-time observation of signing. When it was already signed, the handbook directs the person to sign again above or below the previous signature in the notary's presence. The affirmation option accommodates a person who does not wish to use religious swearing.

sections.heading: Describe each event accurately
sections.body: After the act, complete the appropriate certificate with the proper particulars, signature, expiration information and official impression. A jurat records the sworn or affirmed procedure. An acknowledgment records the different declaration about execution. The customer's payment and the notary's opinion of the document cannot replace either required ceremony.

faqs.q: Can acknowledgment concern yesterday's signature?
faqs.a: Yes, with the present appearance and acknowledgment procedure.

faqs.q: Does silent observation administer a truth oath?
faqs.a: No. The signer must actually make the required oath or affirmation.

articles.keyword: Wisconsin representative execution still needs an interest screen
articles.title: Wisconsin representative execution still needs an interest screen
articles.description: Identify the human signer, represented party and separate conflict conditions.
articles.h1: Wisconsin representative execution still needs an interest screen
articles.lede: An officer or executor signs in a defined role, and the notary keeps that role distinct from personal benefit.

sections.heading: Identify the actual representative
sections.body: A company president appears in Racine to execute a record for the corporation. The notary identifies the individual and completes the ceremony appropriate to the requested act. The handbook describes asking whether the person is signing for the corporation and has been duly authorized to do so. A company logo does not identify the human participant.

sections.heading: Show the role in the certificate
sections.body: The representative certificate identifies the individual, role and represented entity or estate. The handbook examples illustrate corporate officers and estate representatives. This accurately describes in what capacity the person acted. It does not guarantee the entity's ability to pay its obligations or make the notary responsible for predicting the transaction's financial outcome.

sections.heading: Check the separate interest issue
sections.body: The handbook prohibits acts where the notary, spouse or domestic partner is a party or has the stated direct beneficial interest. Representative language does not automatically remove an actual benefit. A notary whose related person signs for an entity should therefore examine the conflict conditions separately instead of assuming a business title resolves every impartiality issue.

sections.heading: Keep advice within authority
sections.body: A nonattorney commission does not authorize preparing deeds, contracts, wills or other legal papers for the customer. The notary can describe the available notarial procedure without selecting the customer's legal strategy. When the requested role or certificate needs legal clarification, the customer obtains appropriate instructions before the notary certifies the actual event.

faqs.q: Should the certificate show representative capacity?
faqs.a: Yes. The handbook directs appropriate role wording.

faqs.q: Does a corporate title automatically remove a spouse's direct benefit?
faqs.a: No. The actual party and interest conditions are assessed separately.

articles.keyword: A Wisconsin vital-record request belongs with its custodian
articles.title: A Wisconsin vital-record request belongs with its custodian
articles.description: Recognize the record category before choosing a notarial certificate.
articles.h1: A Wisconsin vital-record request belongs with its custodian
articles.lede: A private purpose and a customer-provided photocopy do not remove the handbook's vital-record boundary.

sections.heading: Recognize the listed records
sections.body: A customer presents a birth certificate and a photocopy at a Wisconsin office. The handbook treats birth, death, divorce, annulment and marriage certificates as vital records for its stated restriction. The notary identifies the source category before deciding whether a proposed certificate could truthfully and lawfully be attached to the material.

sections.heading: Read the copying restriction
sections.body: The handbook expressly addresses both certified and uncertified copies and directs notaries never to notarize vital-record photocopies brought by a person. Ownership of the certificate or a request to charge no fee does not change the category. Making an official-looking substitute also raises the concern the handbook describes about material appearing to be a vital record or copy.

sections.heading: Use the appropriate custodian
sections.body: The handbook directs customers to a state or county vital-record office or comparable government custodian for the appropriate copy. That custodian role differs from the ordinary notary's impartial witness role. A supplier's stamp or a nicely formatted private certificate cannot turn the notary into the official repository issuing the record.

sections.heading: Do not let labels hide the source
sections.body: A customer may call the request a sworn copy statement or attach a new title page. The notary still recognizes that the proposed work concerns the vital-record photocopy described in the handbook. Explain the boundary and the custodian route while avoiding legal advice about which substitute will satisfy a particular proceeding or foreign recipient.

faqs.q: Does the handbook limit the warning to certified copies?
faqs.a: It expressly discusses certified and uncertified vital-record copies.

faqs.q: Where does it direct customers for appropriate copies?
faqs.a: The official state, county or comparable vital-record custodian.

articles.keyword: A Wisconsin platform change must preserve earlier remote recordings
articles.title: A Wisconsin platform change must preserve earlier remote recordings
articles.description: Plan training for the new system and continuing access to the old archive.
articles.h1: A Wisconsin platform change must preserve earlier remote recordings
articles.lede: Technology-provider approval does not guarantee identical storage services or automatic record migration.

sections.heading: Compare the service models
sections.body: A Wisconsin remote notary considers replacing a platform used for commercial closings. DFI's guide explains that approved providers vary in business model, eligibility and service offerings. Some preserve recordings for the full seven years, while others expect the notary to download and retain them. An approved badge does not answer every storage question in a particular contract.

sections.heading: Preserve the existing recordings
sections.body: The guide requires audiovisual recordings of ordinary RON acts and at least seven years of retention. The notary remains ultimately responsible when a provider or repository stores them. Before closing the former account, determine how the earlier files remain available, how long they will be kept and how the notary can retrieve them after the business relationship ends.

sections.heading: Train on the new provider
sections.body: Wisconsin permits changing providers and using multiple approved providers at the same time. Each provider used requires its own onboarding and training. Familiarity with the former interface does not establish competence on a new system's identity proofing, record confirmation and execution tools. The provider also supplies the authorization notification used for DFI's public database update.

sections.heading: Keep confidentiality during transfer
sections.body: The guide imposes confidentiality on the notary and provider, with separate written consent or specified necessary legal-process grounds for disclosure. Moving an archive for lawful retention should be handled consistently with that requirement. Cancellation does not convert customer recordings into marketing material or authorize public release simply because the provider no longer hosts new appointments.

faqs.q: Does provider cancellation end retention?
faqs.a: No. The required recording period continues.

faqs.q: Does training transfer automatically to every platform?
faqs.a: Complete onboarding and training for each provider used.

articles.keyword: Knowing a Wisconsin remote signer does not remove every safeguard
articles.title: Knowing a Wisconsin remote signer does not remove every safeguard
articles.description: Apply the personal-knowledge exception to its actual purpose.
articles.h1: Knowing a Wisconsin remote signer does not remove every safeguard
articles.lede: DFI's ordinary RON guidance distinguishes identity proofing from the other parts of the act.

sections.heading: Establish genuine personal knowledge
sections.body: A long-standing customer asks a Wisconsin notary to complete an ordinary remote acknowledgment. The guide allows an identity-proofing exception when dealings with the individual give reasonable certainty of claimed identity. The notary assesses actual familiarity. A familiar profile photograph or repeated email address alone should not be mistaken for the sufficient-dealings condition.

sections.heading: Keep the live procedure intact
sections.body: The notary remains physically in Wisconsin and uses the approved technology and provider-specific training for ordinary RON. The method allows simultaneous communication and confirmation that the notary has the same record the person signed or addressed. A personal-knowledge identity route does not remove those separate communication and record safeguards.

sections.heading: Capture and retain performance
sections.body: The guide requires audiovisual recording and at least seven years of retention for ordinary RON. The personal-knowledge exception concerns identity proofing, so it does not authorize omission of the recording. A saved copy of a customer's earlier email cannot show how the current acknowledgment and certificate procedure actually took place.

sections.heading: Use the proper certificate
sections.body: The certificate identifies use of communication technology along with the proper act particulars. If the document instead belongs to the listed estate-planning category, the separate Part 3 procedure must be assessed. The guide's exceptions and alternative routes are each read in their own scope, preventing one satisfied condition from being treated as a waiver of the remaining procedure.

faqs.q: Does personal knowledge eliminate ordinary RON recording?
faqs.a: No. Recording and retention remain separate requirements.

faqs.q: Does knowing the signer allow the notary to work from another state?
faqs.a: No. The notary must still be physically in Wisconsin.

articles.keyword: Wisconsin remote estate planning uses a supervised signing process
articles.title: Wisconsin remote estate planning uses a supervised signing process
articles.description: Recognize the special participants, locations and visible execution requirements.
articles.h1: Wisconsin remote estate planning uses a supervised signing process
articles.lede: The remote estate procedure differs materially from an ordinary approved-provider RON appointment.

sections.heading: Route the document
sections.body: A Wisconsin customer requests remote notarization of a health-care power of attorney. DFI's guide lists powers of attorney and other estate-planning categories within the special Part 3 treatment, with the particular limited real-estate financial-power exception identified elsewhere. The notary checks the actual category before assuming the ordinary RON provider process governs every video request.

sections.heading: Arrange the required people
sections.body: A Wisconsin attorney in good standing supervises the signing and may also serve as notary when properly commissioned. The technology supports interactive real-time audiovisual participation, with the stated accessibility allowance. Unlike ordinary RON, this estate procedure does not require a provider approved through the Part 2C process, while the special safeguards still apply.

sections.heading: Confirm the Wisconsin locations
sections.body: Both the notary and the remote individual are physically in Wisconsin during the signing and make the described attestations. A Wisconsin mailing address does not meet that condition while the signer is visiting another state. This additional signer-location limit is an important difference from ordinary RON's treatment of an out-of-state customer.

sections.heading: Observe the required declarations
sections.body: The individual identifies others present, displays the estate document and confirms page count and signature page, declares age eighteen or older and voluntary execution, then signs so the notary and attorney can see it. The record indicates use of section 140.147. Follow the later document-handling and compliance-affidavit steps rather than treating the end of the call as the end of the entire procedure.

faqs.q: Must the remote estate individual be in Wisconsin?
faqs.a: Yes, the special procedure requires that physical location.

faqs.q: Must the supervising attorney always be a different person from the notary?
faqs.a: No. The guide permits the qualified supervising attorney to serve as notary.

articles.keyword: After a Wisconsin remote estate signing, document handling continues
articles.title: After a Wisconsin remote estate signing, document handling continues
articles.description: Follow the listed original-or-copy route and the attorney's compliance record.
articles.h1: After a Wisconsin remote estate signing, document handling continues
articles.lede: The special procedure includes post-communication steps that connect the signed original and notarized evidence.

sections.heading: Select a listed material route
sections.body: After the special Wisconsin estate communication, the guide permits notarizing an identical copy of the original unsigned record, a signed copy forwarded by the individual or attorney, or the original signed document forwarded by the supervising attorney. These are particular options in the special procedure. The notary checks which version arrived and how it corresponds to the record actually used in the signing.

sections.heading: Return it to the attorney
sections.body: Send the notarized estate document to the supervising attorney, who retains the signed original and any notarized copy. The guide notes that the original and notarized copy together constitute a single document under the cited provisions. A software download alone does not identify where the original and relevant counterparts have gone or who is preserving them.

sections.heading: Complete the sworn compliance record
sections.body: The supervising attorney completes the affidavit of compliance substantially in the statutory form described in the guide. It identifies the participants and addresses, actual Wisconsin signing locations, identity basis, other people present, declarations, observed signing and audiovisual technology. It also documents forwarding and counterpart compilation when relevant, along with the attorney's professional identification.

sections.heading: Address other affidavit requirements
sections.body: Another estate-execution law may require an affidavit with additional information. The guide recognizes combining the required information into one affidavit where the statute permits. Combination is a way to include all necessary statements. It should not be treated as a reason to omit the separate facts needed to describe how the remote execution and notarial process complied with the governing requirements.

faqs.q: Who retains the signed original and notarized copy in the described procedure?
faqs.a: The supervising attorney.

faqs.q: Can a combined affidavit omit information required by another applicable provision?
faqs.a: No. The permitted combination includes the information required by both provisions.
